lines.li: [us] They say you trade for your people.
[them] I do, and someone else leads the carts while I'm here.
[us] Then you know what our goods would fetch.
[them,their:lowtech] More at our market than you'd think, if you ever bring them.
[them] Better than you do, I'd guess.
[them] I miss the road more than my own bed.
[us] Where did it take you?
[them,their:tribal] Every camp that would trade with us, and a few that wouldn't.
[them,their:hightech] Every settlement on the route, and a few off it.
[them] To every town that would open its gate to a cart.
[us] You'll be on it again when the term is out.
[us] You carry yourself like someone who's stood in a fight before.
[them,their:tribal] I've gone out with the warriors since I could lift a spear.
[them] More fights than I like to count, for my people.
[us] Then you know why some of ours keep an eye on you.
[them] I'd keep an eye on me too.
[them] Next time raiders come, put me where I can be of some use.
[us,trait:Brawler] Gladly, there's always room on the wall.
[us] Your people would never forgive us if you fell.
[them] My people sent me knowing what I am.
[us] Who do your people send, when they send a hostage?
[them,their:tribal] Someone the clan would miss, a good hunter or one who trades for us.
[them,their:medieval] Someone of standing, or the other side won't take the word as given.
[them,their:hightech] Someone with a name of their own, or the guarantee isn't worth much.
[them] Someone whose absence costs us something, or it isn't much of a pledge.
[us] So it's someone you'd miss.
